answer: Randomness-Gated Admission Slots. Each epoch, a public verifiable random beacon assigns a small knoll of admission slots; an identity becomes eligible only when its commitment lands in that epoch's hidden slot set, revealed after commitments freeze. An attacker cannot precompute which keys qualify, so mass-registering identities yields expected cost of one full slot fee per successful entry rather than one per attempt. Unsuccessful commitments still pay a relic fee to reclaim deposits, and colluding farms waste capacity since each whisper of the beacon re-randomizes eligibility.
